note: Evidence for Task 19. Task 18 created and edited no manuscript version.

findings.verified_result: Pooled temporal payoff AUC gain +0.0604 decomposes, pair-weighted, into a within-calendar-year contribution of +0.00109 (1.81%) and a between-year contribution of +0.05935 (98.19%). The within-year stratum gain is +0.0064 and the between-year stratum gain +0.0717. 82.81% of the case-control pairs cross year boundaries. Facility-level horizon AUC gaps are -0.0006, +0.0002, +0.0017 and +0.0031 at 12/24/36/60 months. A user-side audit run at month granularity reports a within-month gain of -0.00040 over 55 supported months.
findings.required_manuscript_change: Restate the payoff AUC result as predominantly across-period ranking. Report the pair-weighted contribution shares (1.81% within, 98.19% between), distinguishing them from the stratum-gain magnitudes. Report the facility-level horizon AUCs. Remove any phrasing implying improved ordering of mortgages.
allowed_language: M2 ranks calendar periods more sharply than M1; within calendar periods its payoff ordering of risk intervals is essentially unchanged.
Within-period comparisons contribute 1.81% of the pooled gain; between-period comparisons contribute 98.19%.
Calendar-period ranking can be useful predictive information, but it is not facility-level discrimination.
prohibited_language: improved payoff ranking (unqualified)
ordered payoff-prone observations more effectively
facility-level discrimination improvement
a facility-level ranking gain was structurally unavailable by construction
within-period movement accounts for 10.5% of the pooled gain
findings.residual: Calendar-month granularity unexecuted; requires local frozen arrays.

findings.verified_result: Task 17's structural argument is refuted. In a multinomial softmax with a no-event reference, a month-constant shift is not a monotone transform of a single cause probability because the competing-cause constant enters each facility's own normalizer. Worked counterexample supplied. M2 is additionally a joint refit, so its non-macro coefficients differ from M1's.
findings.required_manuscript_change: Do not use the structural argument. The between-period conclusion must rest on the SA01 decomposition alone. Task 17's report must be annotated as containing a refuted structural claim.
allowed_language: The gain is empirically between-period, as the decomposition shows.
prohibited_language: Month-constant terms cannot change within-month ranking.
structurally unavailable by construction
A within-month gain was unavailable because interactions are prohibited.
findings.residual: None. Task 17 requires an erratum annotation.

findings.verified_result: M2's 2020 mean predicted monthly payoff probability is 0.10048 against an observed 0.02212, a 4.54x over-prediction, and its across-year predicted spread ratio is 56x against M1's 1.44x. M2's across-year ordering of yearly rates is slightly worse than M1's, 0.786 against 0.821. Because AUC is scale-free, an exaggerated between-period spread can raise between-period concordance while proper scores penalise it.
findings.required_manuscript_change: Offer the shared-cause reading as a diagnostic interpretation, clearly labelled, not as a finding. The decomposition result stands independently of it.
allowed_language: A scale-free metric can reward an exaggerated between-period spread that proper scores penalise; the frozen diagnostics are consistent with the 2020 over-prediction driving both.
Selecting on AUC alone would risk rewarding behaviour that destroys the probability estimates.
prohibited_language: the ranking gain and the probability failure are two readings of one phenomenon (as an established finding)
one 2020 over-prediction explains the entire AUC gain
ranking and probability quality diverged independently

findings.verified_result: The per-year decomposition reconciles to the frozen paired delta to 2.7e-15. Calendar 2020 contributes +0.01440 of +0.01612, i.e. 89.34%, on 20.81% of evaluation intervals. 2021 reverses sign at -0.00608. Six of the seven non-2020 years retain positive deltas.
findings.required_manuscript_change: Add the per-year decomposition table to the main text with weights, deltas and contributions.
allowed_language: The deterioration is highly concentrated in calendar 2020, which supplies 89.3% of the aggregate difference.
The deterioration is not exclusive to 2020: six of seven remaining years retain positive differences.
2021 is the one evaluation year in which the macro-augmented model scores better.
prohibited_language: COVID caused the failure.
The deterioration is purely a pandemic artifact.
Macro augmentation worsened temporal probability quality across 2019-2026 (unqualified)

findings.verified_result: Two distinct quantities have been called ex-2020. The contribution residual is +0.00172, which is what Task 17 reported. The renormalised ex-2020 evaluation delta is +0.00217. Relative deterioration is 18.1% full period against 2.8% excluding 2020. The seven-block year sensitivity interval is [-0.00151, +0.00671] and includes zero.
findings.required_manuscript_change: Report the renormalised ex-2020 evaluation delta of +0.00217 and the 2.8% relative figure, and state which of the two quantities is being used. The seven-block interval may be reported as sensitivity only, with its coverage limitation.
allowed_language: Excluding calendar 2020 the difference falls to +0.00217, a 2.8% relative deterioration against 18.1% for the full period.
A seven-block year-level sensitivity interval includes zero; with seven blocks, one of them partial, this is sensitivity information rather than inference.
prohibited_language: The result survives exclusion of 2020 (as a robustness claim)
The ex-2020 difference is statistically significant.
ex-2020 residual of +0.00172 (without saying which quantity that is)

findings.verified_result: On the unseen-vintage population the primary decision metric reverses: M2 joint log loss 0.069811 against M1 0.070631, a delta of -0.000819, on 17,352 facilities and 652,508 intervals. Payoff AUC rises 0.552 to 0.737. M2's payoff calibration slope is better there, 0.529 against 0.347. Payoff Brier still favours M1 at +0.000465, an order of magnitude smaller than the seen population's +0.004698, and default AUC still favours M1.
findings.required_manuscript_change: Report the unseen-vintage comparison in full, including the reversal and the metrics that still favour M1. Restate the study-level conclusion as population-dependent transport. Candidate explanations must be labelled as hypotheses.
allowed_language: Transport behaviour is population-dependent: severe joint-loss deterioration in the seasoned seen-vintage cohort, slight joint-loss improvement with persistent but much smaller cause-Brier deterioration in the younger unseen cohort.
The deterioration cannot be stated at study level; it is a property of the evaluated seen-vintage survivor cohort.
prohibited_language: Macro augmentation worsened temporal probability quality in this study (unqualified)
The unseen-vintage population confirms the primary finding.
Younger loans explain the reversal (as a demonstrated cause)
findings.residual: Per-year decomposition of the unseen-vintage population not frozen.

findings.verified_result: At least 99.93% of CIF landmark entries occur in calendar 2019 (5,615 of 5,619 facilities carry risk intervals in the 2019 cell), and zero truncation at the 60-month horizon bounds every entry at or before 2021-03 under the frozen mask entry + h - 1 <= ordinal('2026-02'). A user-side audit measuring the distribution reports 99.02% entering in the single month 2019-01, with the latest entry in 2020-01.
findings.required_manuscript_change: Replace 'historical rolling macro paths' with language naming a single realised trajectory. State the entry concentration and the calendar span of the paths. Retain the correct existing statement that these are retrospective evaluations, not forecasts.

the realised 2019-2021 macro trajectory
retrospective sequential mapping, not a prospective forecast
prohibited_language: historical rolling macro paths (plural, implying dispersion)
averaged over diverse historical paths
each interval uses information available at its own assessment date (as evidence of path diversity)

findings.verified_result: The 24-month paths are overlapping windows whose union spans roughly 2019-01 to 2021-11 under calendar-2019 entry, and every such window contains most or all of calendar 2020. With the audit's measured entry concentration the dominant window is 2019-01 to 2020-12, containing calendar 2020 entirely. The 24-month CIF comparison and the 2020 calendar deterioration are therefore not statistically independent.
findings.required_manuscript_change: Remove the 24-month CIF from the abstract as an independent third finding. Present it as the cumulative-incidence consequence of the same 2020 over-prediction, and state the non-independence explicitly.
allowed_language: The cumulative-incidence discrepancy is the consequence of the same monthly over-prediction, propagated through the survival recursion over the same calendar period.
The CIF comparison and the 2020 calendar result are two views of one period in one cohort.
prohibited_language: These results demonstrate (three findings presented as mutually corroborating)
independent corroboration from cumulative incidence

findings.verified_result: All four frozen horizons: observed payoff CIF 0.1330/0.3367/0.5056/0.6094 against M2 0.1222/0.7581/0.8079/0.8187 and M1 0.1385/0.2587/0.3536/0.4860. At 12 months M2's absolute error is 0.01081 against M1's 0.00547, so M1 is closer by a factor of 1.98, but both are of the same order and no qualitative failure appears. Observed default CIF 0.0061/0.0360/0.0417/0.0467 against M1 0.0060/0.0107/0.0144/0.0193: all models under-predict default incidence from 24 months onward.
findings.required_manuscript_change: Present all four horizons and both causes in one table.
allowed_language: At the shortest horizon neither model fails qualitatively; M1 is nonetheless about twice as accurate as M2 there.
The discrepancy emerges from 24 months onward as the monthly error compounds.
All three models under-predict observed default incidence beyond 12 months, by roughly a factor of 3.4 at 24 months; this is a baseline limitation, not specific to macro augmentation.
prohibited_language: At 12 months M2 is closer to observed than M1.
The 24-month comparison characterises the models' cumulative-incidence behaviour.
M1 provides an acceptable cumulative-incidence baseline.
